questions.subject: NLP
questions.question: Explain the difference between word embeddings and attention mechanism in NLP.
questions.ideal_answer: word embeddings and attention mechanism differ in several ways: word embeddings is dense vector representations (works by sentiment similarity in vector space) whereas attention mechanism is context-aware weighting (works by focusing on relevant input parts). word embeddings is typically used for Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText, while attention mechanism is used for soft alignment between encoder and decoder. Example demonstrating word embeddings: king - man + woman ≈ queen. Example demonstrating attention mechanism: Bahdanau attention, Luong attention.

questions.question: Explain the difference between named entity recognition and sentiment analysis in NLP.
questions.ideal_answer: named entity recognition and sentiment analysis differ in several ways: named entity recognition is entity extraction task (works by identifying proper nouns) whereas sentiment analysis is opinion polarity detection (works by positive/negative/neutral classification). named entity recognition is typically used for BIO tagging, CRF, transformer-based, while sentiment analysis is used for lexicon-based, ML, deep learning approaches. Example demonstrating named entity recognition: B-PER, I-PER, O tags. Example demonstrating sentiment analysis: fine-grained: aspect-based sentiment.
